keys.statement: Measured reactive residue curves for acetic acid + 1-butanol over an acid resin run towards butyl acetate. Pure ester can therefore be taken as the bottom product of a reactive column, beyond the equilibrium conversion.

plain.title: Butyl acetate reactive column: the ester can be taken pure as bottom product
plain.when: Esterification of acetic acid with 1-butanol over an acid resin stops at equilibrium in a reactor.
plain.do: Use reactive distillation with butyl acetate as the bottom product.
plain.why: Water and the other light products are removed continuously, which drives the reaction on; the ester is the heaviest component, so the residue curves run towards it.
plain.check: Orjuela et al. 2006 measured this in a laboratory batch still at 560 mmHg, not a continuous column: confirm it in a column simulation.
plain.result: Measured reactive residue curves (paths of a boiling, reacting liquid) end at butyl acetate, beyond the equilibrium conversion.

decisions.obstacle: Esterification stops at equilibrium in a reactor.
decisions.mechanism: Removing water and other light products continuously drives the reaction; the ester is the heaviest.
decisions.operation: Reactive distillation with ester as bottoms.
limits: Laboratory batch still at 560 mmHg, not a continuous column.

keys.statement: Scan the catalyst load in reactive residue-curve tests: above a certain load the curves stop changing, which marks the chemical-equilibrium regime. For this resin that was about 8 g, near 0.8 wt% sulfuric-acid equivalent.

plain.title: Find the catalyst load where the reaction reaches equilibrium: raise it until the residue curves stop moving
plain.when: You do not know whether kinetics or equilibrium governs a reactive distillation.
plain.do: Scan the catalyst load in reactive residue-curve tests and increase it until the curves no longer change.
plain.why: At high catalyst load the reaction keeps pace with vaporisation, which marks the chemical-equilibrium regime.
plain.check: Treat the found load as the lowest at which a design may assume equilibrium.
plain.result: For this resin about 8 g, near 0.8 wt% sulfuric-acid equivalent (Orjuela et al. 2006).

decisions.obstacle: Not knowing whether kinetics or equilibrium governs.
decisions.mechanism: At high catalyst load the reaction keeps pace with vaporisation.
decisions.operation: Increase catalyst load until the residue curves no longer move.
decisions.expected_change: A known equilibrium regime for design.

keys.statement: In the reactive still, water and acetic acid stayed in the liquid while butanol was depleted, because water and acid are fully miscible and both bind to the resin. Butanol and the ester instead form two liquid phases with water.

plain.title: Butyl acetate reactive still: butanol runs short while acid and water stay in the liquid
plain.when: Reactants deplete unevenly in the liquid of an acetic acid and butanol reaction over a resin.
plain.do: Account for the acid and water held in the catalyst when you set the feed ratio.
plain.why: Water and acetic acid are fully miscible and both bind to the resin; butanol and the ester instead form two liquid phases with water.
plain.check: Compare the liquid reactant ratio with the fed ratio in your test or simulation.

decisions.obstacle: Uneven depletion of reactants in the column liquid.
decisions.mechanism: Acid-water miscibility and sorption on the resin.
decisions.operation: Account for acid and water held in the catalyst when setting the feed ratio.
